L01.text: Right now, you're spinning around with the Earth at up to sixteen hundred and seventy kilometers an hour. So what if it just stopped?

L02.text: Stop it suddenly, and everything not bolted to the bedrock keeps going east. You, your house, and the ocean.

L03.text: Luckily, nothing can stop a planet that fast. Unluckily, let's slow it down gently instead.

L04.text: Spinning is why Earth bulges in the middle. It's about twenty-one kilometers fatter at the equator.

L05.text: Stop the spin, and that bulge sinks. The oceans slide downhill, toward the poles.

L06.text: Two giant polar oceans. Most of Europe and Russia, underwater.

L07.text: And around the middle, one brand new supercontinent, wrapped around the whole planet.

L08.text: Then there's the Sun. With no spin, one day lasts a whole year. Six months of daylight, then six months of night.

L09.text: Your alarm clock would be very confused.

L10.text: Here's the thing: Earth really is slowing down. The Moon's tides work like a brake.

L11.text: One point four billion years ago, a day lasted just over eighteen hours.

L12.text: So if today felt long, technically, it was.
